newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on late profit-taking.

text.p: Late heavy profit-taking erased Taiwan share prices' early gains on Friday, handing the recently hot index a lower close as its drive toward heavy resistance at 9,600 points put investors in a selling mood, brokers said.
Brokers said the Philippine peso's plunge had no impact on Taiwan's market.
Taiwan's weighted index once surged as high as 9,526.74, a seven-year intraday high, but faded rapidly near the close to end at 9,394.63, a loss of 35.11 points or 0.37 percent.
Turnover was extremely heavy at T$232.9 billion, second only to an all-time high T$251 billion reached on June 19.
"Profit-taking was well expected," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities. "After the big recent surge, apparently the upward momentum was insufficient to break heavy resistance at 9,600."

Electronics, which jumped at the open and once stood more than 2.5 percent higher to lead the wider market's gains, encountered heavy profit-taking and settled at the end for a gain of just 0.27 percent.

Computer giant Acer fell T$2.5 to T$92. Microchip maker Macronix managed to rise T$2.5 to T$72 after saying on Thursday it would invest more than T$200 billion over 10 years to build advanced 12-inch wafer fabrication plants.
Microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor was up T$3.5 to T$130.5.
"Buying is focused squarely on electronics, Taiwan's king industry, especially after so many big expansion plans have been announced," said indepedent analyst Michael Hung.

"Electronics really have risen a lot recently, but when you consider that U.S. over-the-counter share Dell Computer has rocketed 7,416 percent in the past 10 years, you wouldn't say the recent gains in Taiwan electronics have reached their ceilings," Hung said.
